situations.title: Payment service failing in production during the API migration
situations.summary: The API migration uncovered a payment-service dependency that is now causing intermittent checkout failures for ~3% of live users. Tom needs a decision: roll back the partial migration (safer, costs ~2 weeks) or push a hotfix (faster, riskier).
situations.what_changed: Started the morning as a routine '60% done, no blockers' update (#2), became a flagged dependency issue (#9), then escalated into a live production incident affecting real transactions with a one-hour decision window (#16).
situations.recommendation: Get on a call with Tom now. Default to the rollback unless he can validate the hotfix in minutes — you're losing real revenue and a botched hotfix on live payments is the worse failure mode. Two weeks of migration slippage is recoverable; eroding checkout trust is not.
situations.drafted_response: Tom — call me in 5. My instinct is to roll back and protect checkout while we regroup, even at the cost of two weeks, unless you're confident the hotfix is safe and can be validated fast. Walk me through the risk on the hotfix and let's decide together on the call.

situations.title: Northwind deal terms cut in half by their legal team
situations.summary: Priya closed Northwind at 120k ARR on a 2-year contract this morning, but their legal team has come back refusing the 2-year term — they want 1 year with an option to renew, which drops the deal to 60k ARR. They expect an answer by end of day.
situations.what_changed: Announced as a win (120k ARR, 2-year) at 10:45 (#12); by 12:30 legal had halved it to 60k ARR on a 1-year term and put a same-day clock on the answer (#19).
situations.recommendation: Accept the 1-year with a renewal option — a 60k logo landed on April 1st with a renewal path beats a stalled negotiation, and it still anchors the relationship. Push only for a modest concession (e.g. auto-renew or a usage commitment) rather than risking the close.
situations.drafted_response: Priya — let's take the 1-year with the renewal option rather than lose momentum, but before we sign, push once for an auto-renewal clause or a small usage commitment so we protect the upside. If they won't move, accept it and lock the April 1st onboarding. Nice work getting them this far.

flags.title: Phishing email impersonating account security

flags.recommendation: Do not click the link. Delete and report it to IT, and confirm no one on your team entered credentials. Consider a quick all-staff reminder if this was sent widely.
